title: Raffy Tulfo questions credibility of defense team's witness: Is he a super witness?
summary: Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo on Thursday questioned the credibility of the witness presented by Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team, saying that he's answering questions even outside of his…

blocks.text: Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo on Thursday questioned the credibility of the witness presented by Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team, saying that he's answering questions even outside of his expertise.

On the 44th day of the impeachment trial against the Vice President, the defense panel presented Rainer dela Fuente of AML Consulting PH. He was expected to testify on matters in relation to the Anti-Money Laundering Act and other other related documents.
However, Tulfo seemed bothered with the line of questioning and response between defense lawyer Mark Vinluan and Dela Fuente.

"Is he a super witness, omni witness? Ano bang klaseng witness itong pinepresent ng defense? Pati ba naman amici curiae, pakikialaman niya. Supreme Court... Ombudsman... DOJ... Who is he? Who is this guy?" the senator-judge asked.

(Is he a super witness, omni witness? What kind of witness is the defense presenting? Even amici curiae, he's getting involved in that. Supreme Court... Ombudsman... DOJ... Who is he? Who is this guy?)

"I'm really very, very curious about the qualification of this gentleman para lahat ng topic ay kaya niyang sagutin mula sa kanyang handler, or excuse me, sa defense. I don't think he's capable of answering those questions kasi hindi niya na teritoryo 'yun," Tulfo added.

(I'm really very, very curious about the qualification of this gentleman so that he can answer every topic coming from his handler, or excuse me, from the defense. I don't think he's capable of answering those questions because that's no longer his territory.)
Likewise, Senator-judge Joel Villanueva also shared the same sentiments towards the witness.

"Bagat maaari siyang magbigay ng expert opinion sa kanyang larangan bilang eksperto sa money laundering, hindi naman po siya siguro pwede mag-deklara na mali o invalid yung findings ng AMLA at nasa korte yung pagpapasya kung gaano kabigat yung ebidensya na nilalahad dito," he said.

(Although he may be able to give an expert opinion in his field as an expert on money laundering, he probably shouldn't be declaring that the AMLA's findings are wrong or invalid, and it's up to the court to decide how much weight the evidence presented here carries.)
However, Senator-judge Imee Marcos said that her colleagues must understand how justice should work for both parties.

"Ipapaalala ko lang sa lahat na si Lady Justice o yung babaeng hustisya ay bulag, nakatakip ang mata. Kasi hindi kinakailangan na basahin ng bawat dokumento, alamin ang bawat personalidad dahil pantay-pantay ang timbang sa batas," she said.

(I just want to remind everyone that Lady Justice—or the woman of justice—is blind, her eyes are covered. Because it's not necessary to read every document or know every personality, since the scales under the law are equal.)

While he understands the sentiments of Tulfo and Villanueva, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero said that senator-judges should exercise "more leeway, patience" with the defense panel's presentation.

"We note the manifestations made by all the senator-judges. However, the court cannot dictate nor impinge upon how either party will present their evidence much less dictate their strategy in choosing their respective witnesses. I urge our colleagues to exercise more leeway and patience with the presentation being made by the counsel for the respondent," said Escudero.
But Escudero also told the defense panel to take note of the concerns raised by the senator-judges.

"I ask for the indulgence of our colleagues and ask Atty. Mark to take note of the manifestations made and be sensitive to them to a certain extent in continuing with the direct examination of this witness," said Escudero. — RSJ, GMA News
